description: Use this when the user asks for "sidekick health", whether Sidekick or InDesign is connected, or why InDesign commands fail. Returns Sidekick's health and status: server version/role and the InDesign plugin connection.
name: get_health

connections.description: Live connection state for the current server role

pluginReadyState.description: Primary only: live socket state of the InDesign plugin connection

primaryLinkHeartbeat.description: Secondary only: whether heartbeats from the primary are arriving. none = the primary has not promised any (an earlier-release primary never does), alive = arriving, missed = the primary went silent and this server is taking over

primaryLinkReadyState.description: Secondary only: live socket state of the link to the primary server

promoted.description: Secondary only: whether this server has promoted itself to primary

secondaryCount.description: Primary only: number of connected secondary servers

count.description: Consecutive occurrences of this same error

message.description: Most recent command error message (names the failing hop)

secondsAgo.description: Seconds since this error last occurred

lastError.description: Most recent command error, or null if none this session

lastSuccessfulCommandSecondsAgo.description: Seconds since the last command succeeded, or null if none yet this session

version.description: Connected plugin version (semver), or "unknown" on a secondary server whose primary has not reported it yet

disconnectionReason.description: Why the last connection was rejected, if applicable

probe.description: Live end-to-end probe: runs an inert command through the real path (this server -> primary -> plugin) so health reflects whether commands actually work right now

error.description: Failure reason if the probe did not succeed; names the failing hop

ok.description: Whether a live end-to-end command round-trip to InDesign succeeded

bundledImplementationReason.description: Plain-language explanation of why the shipped copy is standing in

devMode.description: True if running in development mode (SIDEKICK_DEV=1)

pid.description: OS process ID of this MCP server instance

role.description: 'primary' if this instance owns the InDesign connection, 'secondary' if another Sidekick on this machine owns it and this one forwards through it, 'unknown' otherwise. 'secondary' is normal and not a fault: Claude Desktop starts every MCP server twice (one per panel), so half of all sessions are talking to a secondary while InDesign works exactly as usual

servingBundledImplementation.description: Present only when the InDesign tools come from the copy that shipped with this install, because no implementation could be downloaded. The tools work, but they are the install-day versions and will be replaced as soon as the release site is reachable

update.description: What the updater is doing, whether it is working, and what it last did -- one field per question, plus a summary sentence that has already joined them

activity.description: What the updater is doing right now: 'idle' (nothing in progress -- the normal state, whether or not updating is healthy; read problem for that), 'checking' (asking the release site for versions), or 'downloading' (fetching an implementation)

autoUpdateDisabledReason.description: Why automatic updating is off, when it is: development mode (SIDEKICK_DEV=1) or a pinned SIDEKICK_VERSION. Null in normal operation, where updates are automatic

downloadingVersion.description: The version being fetched while activity is 'downloading'; null otherwise

holdReason.description: Why tool calls are held and the remedy (wait, or restart Sidekick); null whenever toolCallsHeld is false

lastCheckSecondsAgo.description: Seconds since the last update check finished, successfully or not, or null if none has run this session (see autoUpdateDisabledReason). This is what dates the rest: a problem recorded hours ago and one from five seconds ago read very differently

lastInstall.description: The implementation install that most recently completed in this session, as a dated event, or null if this session has only ever run what it started with. An install from hours ago is history, not an update waiting to happen -- nothing is ever 'waiting to be installed'; installs apply immediately

problem.description: Why the most recent update attempt failed -- a check that could not reach the release site, or a download that did not complete -- or null while updating is working. A timeout here usually means something on the network is blocking releases.sidekick.eastpole.nl; Sidekick keeps running the implementation it already has either way

summary.description: One plain-language sentence saying what the update machinery is doing, already combining every field below. Quote this rather than re-joining the raw fields -- joining them wrongly is how a resting Sidekick once got reported as having an update waiting

toolCallsHeld.description: Whether InDesign tool calls are being held right now because of an update (a major version change or downgrade in progress, or one that failed). When true, holdReason says why and what to do; when false, tools work regardless of what the other fields report

uptimeSeconds.description: Seconds since this server process started
